issues.span: Since he is left falling short in the welfare of sentient beings, / Their lower realms will be endless.
issues.evidence: The Tibetan subject of དམན་གྱུར་པས is the bodhisattva (བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་ in line 2), whose capacity is diminished; bo-shenga 4-9: "རྒྱལ་བའི་སྲས་དེ་སེམས་ཅན་གྱི་དོན་བྱེད་པ་ལ་དམན་པར་གྱུར་པས། གེགས་བྱེད་པ་པོ་དེ་ཡི་ངན་འགྲོ་ལ་མུ་དང་མཐའ་མེད". English "he" is followed by "Their" and so can be read as the obstructor. Also ངན་འགྲོ is a single rebirth-state (Skt durgatiparyanto), the obstructor's, not plural realms.
issues.fix: Since that bodhisattva is left falling short in the welfare of sentient beings, / The obstructer's lower realm has no end.

issues.span: For those who pervade all of space to its limits, / What need to speak of destroying the happiness of embodied beings?
issues.evidence: Tibetan "ནམ་མཁའ་མ་ལུས་མཐའ་ཀླས་པའི། ལུས་ཅན" is an attributive on ལུས་ཅན: embodied beings who extend to (dwell to) the limits of all space (Skt aśeṣākāśaparyanta-vāsinām; bo-gyaltsab 4-10: "ནམ་མཁའ་མ་ལུས་པའི་མཐའ་ཀླས་པའི་ལུས་ཅན"). The English makes line 3 a dangling "For those who..." that detaches from "embodied beings" and uses "pervade", which the Tibetan/Sanskrit do not say.
issues.fix: Of embodied beings dwelling to the limits of all space, / What need to speak of destroying their happiness?

issues.evidence: རྣམ་ཐར་མི་འགྱུར་ is "will not be released/freed" from the suffering of the lower realm (Skt na vimucyate). bo-gyaltsab 4-22: "ངན་འགྲོ་ལས་རྣམ་པར་ཐར་བར་མི་འགྱུར་ཏེ"; bo-kunpal 4-22: "ངན་སོང་གི་གནས་དེ་ལས་རྣམ་པར་ཐར་པ་མི་འགྱུར"; bo-shenga: "སྡུག་བསྔལ་ལས་རྣམ་པར་ཐར་བར་མི་འགྱུར". "Attain liberation" turns release from that state into attaining the goal of liberation.
issues.fix: One will not be liberated [from it],

issues.span: When I promised this, I myself / Was not freed from afflictions.
issues.evidence: མ་གྲོལ་བ is a state continuing at the time of the vow and now, not a completed past event: bo-shenga 4-41 "གང་ཚེ་བདག་ཉིད་ཀྱང་...ཉོན་མོངས་རྣམས་ལས་མ་གྲོལ་ན"; bo-kunpal "ཉོན་མོངས་པ་རྣམས་ལས་ཅུང་ཟད་ཙམ་ཡང་མ་གྲོལ་བར་གནས་ན". The verse is a clause continuing into the next verse. The English past finite "Was not freed" closes it as a past statement.
issues.fix: When I promised this, I myself / Was still not free from afflictions,

issues.evidence: བྱད་མ is glossed by bo-kunpal 5-4 as "ཕ་རོལ་པོའི་མཐུས་རྦད་པའི་བྱད་མ་གདོན་རྦད་འདྲེ་རྦོད་གཏོང": harmful spirits/hexes sent by another's power, not human witches. "Witches" (Skt ḍākinyaḥ) suggests human sorceresses.

འདི་ལྟར here introduces the reason for the preceding claim (Skt yasmāt "since"); bo-gyaltsab 5-6: "རྒྱུ་མཚན་འདི་ལྟར། ཚེ་འདི་དང་ཕྱི་མའི་འཇིགས་པ་ཐམས་ཅད་དང་...སེམས་ཉིད་ལས་བྱུང་བ་ཡིན". English "Thus" reads as a conclusion drawn from what precedes, reversing the direction of the argument.

issues.span: From what did those groups of women arise?
issues.evidence: The Tibetan as given reads "མེ་ཚོགས" (masses of fire), which bo-shenga 5-7 follows ("མེ་ཚོགས་དེ་དག་རྒྱུ་ཅི་ལས་བྱུང་"). The English follows the variant "མོ་ཚོགས" (bo-kunpal "མོ་ཡི་ཚོགས"; bo-gyaltsab 5-8 calls མེ་ཚོགས a corrupt reading; Skt striyaḥ). English does not render the Tibetan as given, so the textual choice should be marked.
issues.fix: From what did those groups of women (var. masses of fire) arise?

issues.span: Whatever the result of generating a single clear mind, / Such as Brahmā and so forth,
issues.evidence: Tibetan "འབྲས་བུ་གང་། ཚངས་ལ་སོགས་པ་ཡིན་པ་ལྟར" means: just as the result of generating a single clear mind is (rebirth as) Brahmā etc. Brahmā is the result, not an example of a mind, and the comparison marker ལྟར is lost; bo-shenga 5-15: "འབྲས་བུ་གང་། ཚངས་པ་ལ་སོགས་པའི་གནས་སུ་སྐྱེ་བ་ཡིན་པ་ལྟར". "Such as" makes the lines read as a list of examples of results/minds.
issues.fix: Just as the result of generating a single clear mind / Is [rebirth as] Brahmā and so forth,
